why: Mathis gives 1460 x 8 x sqrt(1.5) / (0.08 x sqrt(0.001)) = 5,654,600 bit/s, under the window's 65,536 x 8 / 0.08 = 6,553,600, so loss binds; 5.6546 Mbit/s of 1000 is 0.565%, two figures 0.57%.

name: the defaults, how it was worked out: the window and the loss model, named

fields.label: Receive window
fields.note: One window in flight, then a full round trip waiting for its acknowledgement: window / RTT.

fields.label: Packet loss
fields.note: MSS x 1.22 / (RTT x sqrt(loss)), Mathis et al.: a Reno-style sender that halves its window on every loss. CUBIC and BBR do better on long paths.

name: the defaults: an 80ms path where loss and a 64KB window nearly tie: what fixing it buys
why: Loss at which Mathis meets the window's 6,553,600 bit/s: (1460 x 8 x sqrt(1.5) / (0.08 x 6,553,600))^2 = 0.000744, so 0.074%. The link's bandwidth-delay product is 1e9 x 0.08 / 8 = 10,000,000 B = 9.54 MB, and the loss for it (14,304 / 80,000,000)^2 = 3.2e-8, 0.0000032%, one in 31 million.

fields.label: Cut loss below 0.074%
fields.note: Then the receive window is the limit.

fields.label: To fill the link
fields.note: A window of at least 9.54 MB, and loss below 0.0000032%, about one packet in 31 million.
